subject: Hosted to Dedicated — Migration Sanity Checklist & Rollback Milestones
messages:
From: Tim Choi <tim.choi@helios.ai>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procure@helios.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted → Dedicated migration kickoff + initial asks

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier today. Helios is ready to start scoping the Hosted→Dedicated migration that will coincide with our Q3 launch. To help our procurement and SRE teams, can you share a concise checklist that outlines the sizing validation steps, the production cutover windows you recommend, and the rollback milestones if traffic needs to be shifted back to Hosted? I attached our initial traffic estimates (helios_migration_req.xlsx).

High level constraints from our side:
- Production SLA target: 95th pct < 200ms token latency
- Peak qps (text-gen): ~220 concurrent streams, median seq len 320 tokens
- Data residency: US-only, must run in our reserved VPC

Procurement will want an estimate of the committed GPU-hours and the migration blackout windows so they can get approvals. Can we target a short call early next week with engineering to align?

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Choi
Head of AI Platform, Helios AI

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Choi <tim.choi@helios.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted → Dedicated migration kickoff + initial asks

Tim — good ask, we can get that over to you.

Quick plan:
1) Sizing validation: run a short preflight in our staging Dedicated cluster with a production-like traffic replay (2 hours) to validate throughput, KV-cache hit rates, and tail latency. We'll produce a "sizing matrix" with commit recommendation (GPU type + count + quantization profile).
2) Cutover windows: recommend a two-step cutover (warm-swap + full-swap) in a 48h launch window to minimize risk. Warm-swap (traffic split 10/90) for validation, full-swap only after acceptance gates.
3) Rollback milestones: define three stop conditions (latency regression, token-error rate, throughput shortfall) and an immediate fallback policy at 1 hour after a triggered stop condition.

I'll attach a template checklist and propose internal owners. Marissa — please draft the migration playbook sections (runbooks + acceptance gates). Ben — can you scope the GPU footprint baseline? Karthik — please list the required network/VPC artifacts for Helios Private deployment.

Proposed time for the alignment call: Mon 2026-04-13 10:00 PT. Works for you?

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_sizing_matrix_v2.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted → Dedicated migration kickoff + initial asks

Team — notes from the call and action items below. I replayed Helios production traces in staging with the sizing matrix pinned to bfloat16 quantized 8x A100s to start; preliminary numbers:

- Throughput: 220 concurrent streams stable on 6 x A100-80GB with batching configured to 128ms latency budget for 90% of traffic.
- Tail (95th): 180ms average, spikes to 260ms under synthetic load ramps (insufficient KV cache priming).
- Recommendation: 7 x A100-80GB as committed baseline to hit 95th < 200ms under expected warm-cache conditions; keep 1 x burst node for peak scaling.

Acceptance gates for warm-swap (10/90):
- 48-hour staged traffic with no more than 10% increase in token-error rate vs Hosted baseline
- Latency SLO: 95th < 200ms for two consecutive 1-hour windows
- No elevated rate of context-window misses (KV cache hit-rate >= 85%)

Rollback triggers (immediate rollback to Hosted if any occur):
1) Sustained 95th > 250ms for 30 continuous minutes
2) Production token-error increase > 20% vs baseline for 15 minutes
3) Any data-path misrouting or VPC egress policy failures

Attachments: I exported the runbook draft (rollback_runbook.md) and updated sizing workbook (redwood_sizing_matrix_v2.xlsx). Ben, confirm the final GPU-commit wording I should send to Procurement.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted → Dedicated migration kickoff + initial asks

Tim — quick answers and next steps below.

1) Committed GPU-hours & cost band: based on Marissa's preflight, baseline = 7 x A100-80GB (reserved) with 1 x A100 burst node. Rough committed-hours estimate: 7 GPUs * 24h * 30d = 5040 GPU-hours/month. Preliminary committed price band (illustrative): $XX,XXX–$YY,YYY/month (Ben will provide final quoting to Procurement).

2) SLA & DocuSign: Monica will prepare a short SLA addendum covering cutover maintenance windows (we recommend maintenance start only outside 07:00–22:00 PT) and a single-point escalation phone list. We have a standard DocuSign envelope template; we'll create an envelope pre-filled with RDW-HELIOS-PO on the subject and share the link.

3) Rollback timing & session handling: expected timeline from rollback trigger to traffic fully on Hosted is ~18–45 minutes depending on cache warm-up (shorter if KV caches are preserved). For streaming/stateful sessions we detect in-progress streams and:
   - If <=30% of active streams are mid-request, we will allow graceful finish on Hosted if safe; otherwise we cut and restart on Hosted (we'll mark those sessions in postmortem).

Action items:
- Ben: final quote and monthly committed-hours in concrete dollars (by Thu 2026-04-16).
- Monica: DocuSign + SLA addendum draft (by Thu 2026-04-16).
- Karthik: VPC peering checklist and firewall rules required for warm-swap (by Wed 2026-04-15).
- Tim/Procurement: confirm preferred PO number to include in DocuSign envelope.

If that timeline works, we'll circulate a short email for Procurement to approve the GPU commitment and schedule the preflight staging run (2h replay) for the week of Apr 20.

Thanks — Avery
